title: Types of Plate Boundaries
subject: Geography
description: This flowchart categorizes the three main types of plate boundaries (Divergent, Convergent, Transform), detailing their movements, geological features, and examples.
mermaidCode:
graph TD
A[Plate Boundaries] --> B[Divergent (Constructive)]
B --> B1(Plates move apart)
B --> B2(New crust created)
B --> B3(Mid-ocean ridges, rift valleys)
B3 --> B4(East African Rift)
A --> C[Convergent (Destructive)]
C --> C1[Oceanic-Oceanic]
C1 --> C1a(Subduction)
C1 --> C1b(Trenches & volcanic island arcs)
C1b --> C1c(Mariana Trench, Japanese Islands)
C --> C2[Oceanic-Continental]
C2 --> C2a(Subduction)
C2 --> C2b(Deep trenches & volcanic mountain belts)
C2b --> C2c(Andes, Cascade Range)
C --> C3[Continental-Continental]
C3 --> C3a(Collision)
C3 --> C3b(High mountain ranges without volcanism)
C3b --> C3c(Himalayas, Alps)
A --> D[Transform (Conservative)]
D --> D1(Horizontal sliding)
D --> D2(No crust creation or destruction)
D --> D3(San Andreas Fault)
